Definition: from G3326 and G2192; to share or participate; by implication, belong to, eat (or drink):--be partaker, pertain, take part, use.
BiblicalUsage: Christ took part in flesh and blood so He could destroy the devil through death, believers are partakers of one bread at the Lord's table, and they cannot partake of the Lord's table and the table of devils. Sharing is the heart of this word, and Paul draws the line at what we share in.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe partaking is never neutral: we share in Christ's flesh and blood, we share in one bread as one body, and the table we sit at decides whose we are. The table we sit at decides whose we are, and there are only two tables.
